schemes.name: comp19_pinwheel_three_wings_shared_core
schemes.secondary_language: three equal-depth wings radiate from a shared central core, each rotated 120 degrees so the space between them is three equivalent outdoor bays
schemes.formal_principle: 세 날개가 공유 코어에서 120도씩 회전하며 뻗어 나가, 그 사이마다 동등한 외부 공간 세 켜를 만든다.
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; a 120-degree rotation is a 4×4 with determinant +1, so the three-arm plan is a single rule applied twice rather than three placed bars

ops.why: a quarter of the plot length at the full height budget - one arm, slender enough that two rotated copies do not close the spaces between them

the arm is turned 120 degrees twice around the shared core; the tie plate is the core itself, and 'pinwheel' means each unit faces the next one's flank rather than its own twin - the limitation is that the footprint is determined by n and turn, not by a searched plan
the street-facing bay is cut further back so one of the three outdoor spaces reads as the address rather than as one of three equal voids

schemes.name: comp19_stacked_bands_alternating_cantilever
schemes.secondary_language: three unequal horizontal bands stacked on a narrow footprint, each band cantilevering in the opposite direction to the one below
schemes.formal_principle: 세 켜의 밴드가 좁은 발자국 위에 쌓이며 매 켜마다 반대 방향으로 내밀어, 단면이 좌우로 번갈아 기운다.
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the alternating offset is the section, not a sculptural gesture - each band's structural backspan is its own depth, independent of the one above or below

ops.why: three bands on the narrowed axis; contrast 1.25 gives the lower band more footprint than the upper two, which matters for structural grounding

the upper two levels extend toward the open side; reach 0.28 is the tested delivery limit - the limitation is that the same reach applies to both levels rather than alternating, so the alternation is declared by the two-direction stagger below
the top band steps back on the opposite face from the cantilever, completing the alternating cross-section without exceeding the structural gate on either side

schemes.name: comp19_butterfly_bar_notched_at_both_ends
schemes.secondary_language: a deep bar whose roof is a valley section and whose two short ends are both notched, so the V-ridge drains toward each corner
schemes.formal_principle: 깊은 바의 지붕이 골짜기 단면이고 두 짧은 끝은 모두 패여, V자 능선이 각 모서리 쪽으로 흘러내린다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a valley roof between two corner notches
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; a butterfly valley combined with bilateral notching is a section and plan decision that differ from the board's concertina (O9) and folded-plate (comp18)

ops.why: half the plot depth on the short axis gives a genuinely deep bar whose long face is the street front and whose section is the subject
the valley ridge runs the full long axis; pitch 0.5 is 1:2 rise-to-run, shallow enough to be structural on a bar this wide - the section is the base shape
a notch at each short end removes the corner mass that would otherwise hide the valley from the approach; the two cuts also break the street face into a centre and two shoulders

schemes.name: comp19_perimeter_loop_collapsed_to_plinth
schemes.secondary_language: a three-sided perimeter loop whose open wing is replaced by a low plinth, so the court has one low threshold and three high walls
schemes.formal_principle: 세 면의 루프 중 열린 면은 낮은 기단으로 치환되어, 마당은 세 개의 높은 벽과 하나의 낮은 문지방으로 둘러싸인다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: an asymmetric enclosure with one low threshold
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the loop is collapsed rather than closed: the fourth side is present as a plinth rather than absent, which distinguishes this from the U-plan and from the full perimeter court

ops.why: the parcel-scale four-bar loop is the opening; bar 0.22 is deep enough for office rooms on both faces of each wing
the open wing is separated and reduced to half height by contrast 2.0; the three remaining wings stay at full height - this is what collapses the loop into an asymmetric enclosure rather than a U

the low threshold is carved at its centre so the court has a gate rather than a continuous low wall; the limitation is that the carve reduces the plinth area, which may need to be verified against BCR

schemes.name: comp19_cascading_terrace_three_steps_down
schemes.secondary_language: three rectangular terraces of the same width but diminishing depth cascade from the back of the site toward the street, each one a storey lower than the one behind
schemes.formal_principle: 같은 너비의 테라스 세 켜가 대지 안쪽에서 가로 쪽으로 차례로 낮아지며, 뒤켜의 지붕이 앞켜의 마당이 된다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: three cascading steps reading as one section
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the section principle differs from O29 (four alternating shifted mass layers) and O11 (descending three-sided house) because here all three terraces share the same street width and the descent is front-to-back rather than three-sided

ops.why: three bands aligned to the back of the site, contrast 1.6 shrinks each band's depth as it rises - the deepest band is at the bottom and the shallowest at the top, which is the cascade
the stepped roofs are declared as walkable ground - the section is a public staircase and the limitation is that the slope is continuous rather than terraced in plan
a service slot is cut from the back wall of the lowest terrace so the building has two independent entries - street and rear - without splitting the mass

schemes.name: comp19_ground_mat_raised_on_forest_of_piers
schemes.secondary_language: a single near-full-coverage mat of offices is raised to the second storey on a forest of piers; the ground floor is fully public and unenclosed
schemes.formal_principle: 사무실 판 전체가 기둥숲 위 2층으로 올라가 지상층을 막힘 없는 공공 마당으로 내준다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a mat suspended above a free ground
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the pilotis-as-civic-ground proposition differs from O14 (thin elevated roof over three grounded volumes) because the elevated element here is the full programme mat rather than a canopy, and the ground below it is interior civic space rather than landscape

ops.why: half the height budget over a plot-wide plan - the mat at full office depth

the mat is raised to the 38% level, which at floor_height_m 3.8 is approximately one storey of clear civic height under the slab; clearance 0.38 is near the tested gate limit and the limitation is that structure at this clearance requires careful column sizing
two large openings through the mat bring daylight to the ground level below; without them the civic space under a full-BCR plate has no natural light

schemes.name: comp19_tower_twisting_above_compact_podium
schemes.secondary_language: a squat four-storey podium gives up one storey to a slender tower whose plan rotates as it rises
schemes.formal_principle: 낮고 넓은 기단이 탑 하나를 내고, 그 탑은 올라갈수록 평면이 돌아 네 모서리가 사방으로 향한다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a twisting tower above a grounded podium
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the twist is a 4×4 rotation that accumulates per storey; the podium is the structural footing and is not tapered - this differs from O6 (kite-plan units turning and shrinking) because only the upper element rotates and the podium remains orthogonal

ops.why: the podium occupies 62% of the height budget and 100% of the half-plot seed; it is the stable ground element and its height is the plinth for what rises above

a smaller volume is seated inside the podium footprint and rises 85% of its own height above the podium lid; turn 38 degrees rotates the nested tower so its corners point diagonally, which is the visible difference from a straight extension of the podium
the base of the tower is carved from the street face of the podium to open the entry court; the carved void is also the notch that makes the podium-tower junction legible in the elevation

schemes.name: comp19_two_bars_bridged_at_different_levels
schemes.secondary_language: two parallel bars of different height are bridged at two different levels, enclosing a covered street between them
schemes.formal_principle: 높이가 다른 두 바가 서로 다른 레벨에서 두 개의 다리로 이어져, 그 사이에 지붕 덮인 골목이 만들어진다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: two bridges at split levels spanning a covered street
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the split-level bridge differs from O17 (single upper bridge joining two grounded piers) because two bridges at different heights create a section hierarchy in the covered street rather than a single connecting move

ops.why: a quarter of the plot depth at full height budget - one bar, slender enough to stand clear of its mirror
the second bar mirrors the first at the plot's long centreline; the two bars now face each other across a covered slot, and their volume is identical by construction

a bridge at 25% height and one at 55% height connects the two bars at two different storeys; the lower bridge is the entry lobby and the upper bridge is an office floor - the limitation is that the join operator places one bridge and a second call is needed for the second level
the second bridge at 55% height closes the section at a higher level; the two bridges together define the covered street's sectional hierarchy

schemes.name: comp19_fractured_bar_diagonal_hinge
schemes.secondary_language: a single bar is fractured along a diagonal that runs from one short face to the opposite long face, so the two pieces open at one end and close at the other
schemes.formal_principle: 하나의 바가 대각선 힌지로 꺾여 한쪽은 벌어지고 반대쪽은 닫혀, 단면이 쐐기형의 외부 공간을 조각한다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a diagonal fracture opening a wedge void
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the fracture is a single plane cut that generates a wedge void - the spatial content is the wedge, not the two resulting pieces, which distinguishes this from the split-pair (comp18) whose content is the gap between two equal halves

ops.why: half the plot length at the full height budget - a bar long enough that a diagonal cut leaves two usable floor plates on either side

the single diagonal cut at 28 degrees from the long axis produces two pieces whose long edges close at one end and diverge at the other; slot 0 keeps the pieces in contact at the narrow end while the wedge opens on the far side
one piece is slid toward the open face so the wedge opens on the street side; the amount is small so the pieces remain in structural contact at the hinge

schemes.name: comp19_inscribed_court_in_a_full_block
schemes.secondary_language: a near-full-coverage block at medium height has a single court inscribed from the top, deep enough to reach the first floor, so the court is contained on all four sides
schemes.formal_principle: 꽉 찬 매스 상단에서 내부 마당 하나가 1층까지 파고 들어가, 네 면이 모두 닫힌 사면 둘러싸인 마당이 만들어진다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a contained four-sided court carved from a solid
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the inscribed court differs from the standard loop courtyard (which is defined by four separate bars) because the outer mass is a continuous solid from which the court is removed - the structural logic is a hollowed block rather than an assembled ring

ops.why: the full plot at 72% of the height budget - a medium-height solid block that is BCR-limited rather than height-limited, leaving room for the court to read clearly in the section

a court is removed from the top of the block to 55% of its height; the remaining base wraps the court on all four sides and at its floor, which is what distinguishes this from a loop whose base is always ground - the limitation is that 'inscribe' does not guarantee minimum room depth around the perimeter and that must be checked against the parcel geometry
a corridor is cut from the block's street face to the inscribed court so the court is accessible from outside; without this cut the court is a private lightwell rather than a civic courtyard

schemes.name: comp19_radial_wings_facing_shared_centre
schemes.secondary_language: four short wings face a shared open centre without touching, so the centre is defined by what surrounds it rather than by a wall
schemes.formal_principle: 네 개의 짧은 날개가 공유 중심을 마주 보며 서지만 닿지 않아, 중심은 경계 없이 둘러싸인다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: four wings facing a centreless field
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the radial arrangement differs from the four-equal-halls-in-one-frame (comp18) because there is no outer frame and the centre is constituted by the wings' orientations rather than by an enclosing wall

ops.why: four units arranged radially around a shared centre with no tie plate; tie 0.0 means the centre is open ground rather than a connecting slab, and spread 1.55 ensures each wing clears 3.9 m from its neighbours at the gap-gate threshold
each wing has a gable on its short face so it reads as a directed house-form pointing toward the centre - the section confirms the radial orientation that the plan proposes

the outermost face of each wing is partially cut back so the arrival path reads through the wing rather than around it; the limitation is that 'carve' applies once and relies on the radial arrangement to distribute it to each unit's open face

schemes.name: comp19_vertical_extract_beside_its_socket
schemes.secondary_language: a piece is extracted from one flank of a compact block and stood upright beside the socket it left, so the void and the extracted mass read as a pair
schemes.formal_principle: 단단한 매스의 한 측면에서 한 덩어리를 뽑아 그 옆에 세워, 빠진 소켓과 뽑힌 매스가 한 쌍으로 읽힌다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a socket and its extracted piece
schemes.reference_basis: original authorship; the extract operation is a single constructive move (void + extraction) that differs from all carve-and-discard approaches on the board; the spatial content is the legible pairing of absence and presence

ops.why: half the plot at 78% of the height budget - a block whose height is enough that an extracted piece standing beside it is still lower than the parent

a piece of 38% plan size is extracted at ground level and placed 5.2 m clear of the socket; gap 5.2 m clears the 3.9 m rejection threshold with margin, height 0.88 puts the extracted piece above the parent block so the pair reads as plinth and tower rather than as two equal blocks

a narrow bridge at mid-height ties the extracted tower back to the parent block so the pair is one building rather than two independent volumes; the limitation is that the bridge must span the gap without reducing the ground-level passage
